before.title: PToken.claimSurplus has no access control — attacker can claim tokens sent directly to PToken for themselves
before.description: claimSurplus(address who) is public with no caller restriction. Any surplus tokens held by the contract (underlying balance above totalBalances) are credited to the caller-supplied `who` address. A user who sends underlying tokens to PToken without using wrap() loses those tokens to whoever calls claimSurplus first.

steps.finding: wrap() calls safeTransferFrom then claimSurplus(msg.sender) atomically — safe path
claimSurplus is public, takes arbitrary `who`, checks currBalance > totalBalances and credits surplus to `who` — any caller can supply any beneficiary
User directly transfers underlying to PToken contract; attacker front-runs by calling claimSurplus(attacker) in same or subsequent block

claimAssessment.executionContext: Attacker is an external EOA. PToken is a standalone contract (not module-based). msg.sender unrestricted. Victim's tokens are already in the contract.

steps.action: Verify no access control on claimSurplus
steps.expectedResult: Any caller can pass arbitrary `who` and claim all surplus

steps.action: Confirm wrap() is the only intended path and is atomic
steps.expectedResult: wrap() is atomic so no window exists for direct-wrap callers, but direct token transfers remain exploitable
Victim who sends tokens directly to PToken without calling wrap() loses tokens to front-runner calling claimSurplus(attacker_address)

checks.reason: claimSurplus is public, no modifier, callable by any external account
No access control check whatsoever on the caller or the `who` parameter; only requires currBalance > totalBalances
claimSurplus makes no external calls after state writes; no reentrancy path
Attacker pays zero; receives balances[who] += amount credit worth underlying tokens redeemable via unwrap(). Victim funded the surplus.

before.title: Exec.deferLiquidityCheck accepts arbitrary account — attacker can freeze any account's deferLiquidityStatus to block liquidation
before.description: deferLiquidityCheck takes an unconstrained `account` address. An attacker can set any victim account's deferLiquidityStatus to DEFERLIQUIDITY__CLEAN, occupying it for the duration of the callback, potentially blocking a concurrent liquidation that checks this flag.

steps.finding: deferLiquidityCheck takes `account` with no restriction; sets accountLookup[account].deferLiquidityStatus = DEFERLIQUIDITY__CLEAN before callback
Need to verify if liquidation reads deferLiquidityStatus — unresolved without reading liquidation code
Even without blocking liquidation, attacker can pointlessly defer any account; if liquidation respects the defer flag, griefing is feasible

claimAssessment.executionContext: Attacker is external EOA. account param is any address. Callback executes on msg.sender (attacker contract).

steps.expectedResult: Attacker supplies victim address as account

steps.action: Check if Liquidation.sol reads deferLiquidityStatus before proceeding
steps.expectedResult: If yes, liquidation reverts while victim is deferred; if no, griefing is limited

checks.reason: deferLiquidityCheck is external reentrantOK with no restriction on account param

Only guard is deferLiquidityStatus != NONE (reentrancy guard for the same account). No guard requiring account == msg.sender. Whether liquidation.sol checks this flag is not confirmed without reading that file.

Callback fires on attacker-controlled contract. nonReentrant functions (borrow, withdraw) cannot be called because reentrancyLock is already set by an outer call if any; but deferLiquidityCheck is reentrantOK so lock state depends on call path. Missing: Liquidation.sol source.
If liquidation is blocked, victim remains undercollateralized and protocol accrues bad debt. Attacker profit unclear.
